endpoints.name: V1 Requests
endpoints.description: The requests the instance received over a recent window, by user and database. Operational, and useful for finding which client is generating load.

endpoints.name: V1 Statistics
endpoints.description: The instance's internal statistics in the v1 debug format. Operational.

endpoints.name: V1 Query
endpoints.description: Runs an INFLUXQL query against a v1-style database. Requires the database name and the statement. The compatibility endpoint for installations and tools written against InfluxDB 1.x; it returns JSON rather than the CSV the Flux endpoint returns, which is why both exist.

endpoints.name: Authorizations
endpoints.description: The API tokens issued, with their permissions, the organisation and user, and their status. Security inventory -- a token's permission set is what decides which of these endpoints it can reach.

endpoints.name: Authorization
endpoints.description: One authorization by id, with its permissions.

endpoints.name: Metadata Snapshot
endpoints.description: A backup of the instance's metadata. Operational, and returns a binary payload rather than rows.

endpoints.name: TSM Data Snapshot
endpoints.description: A backup of one shard's time series data. Requires a shard id. Binary backup content, not queryable data.

endpoints.name: Buckets
endpoints.description: The buckets on the instance -- the containers time series are written into, each with its organisation and its RETENTION PERIOD. Filterable by name, id and organisation. THE RETENTION PERIOD BOUNDS EVERY QUERY AGAINST A BUCKET: data older than it has been deleted, so an empty result for last year is expected behaviour rather than missing data, and this is the only place that boundary is visible.

endpoints.name: Bucket
endpoints.description: One bucket by id, with its retention rules.

endpoints.name: Bucket Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one bucket. Requires a bucket id.

endpoints.name: Bucket Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one bucket.

endpoints.name: Bucket Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one bucket.

endpoints.name: Source Buckets
endpoints.description: The buckets available through one source. Requires a source id.

endpoints.name: Cell View
endpoints.description: The visualisation configuration of one dashboard cell, INCLUDING THE FLUX QUERY BEHIND IT. Requires the dashboard and cell ids. The map from a chart back to the query producing it, which is the fastest route to a known-good query for a metric.

endpoints.name: Checks
endpoints.description: The monitoring checks defined -- the queries evaluated on a schedule to decide a status. Requires an organisation id. Checks produce statuses, notification rules act on them, and notification endpoints deliver them: the three together are InfluxDB's alerting, and none makes sense alone.

endpoints.name: Check
endpoints.description: One check by id, with its thresholds and schedule.

endpoints.name: Check Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one check.

endpoints.name: Check Query
endpoints.description: The Flux query one check actually runs. Requires a check id. What a check MEANS, as opposed to its name.

endpoints.name: Dashboards
endpoints.description: The dashboards defined, with their cells and the organisation. What the operators actually watch, which is a fair guide to the metrics that matter on this instance.

endpoints.name: Dashboard
endpoints.description: One dashboard by id, with its cells.

endpoints.name: Dashboard Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one dashboard.

endpoints.name: Dashboard Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one dashboard.

endpoints.name: Dashboard Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one dashboard.

endpoints.name: Database Retention Policy Mappings
endpoints.suffix: /api/v2/dbrps?bucketID={Bucket ID?}&db={Database?}&default={Default Filter?:true|false}&id={Mapping ID?}&org={Organization Name?}&orgID={Organization ID?}&rp={Retention Policy?}
endpoints.description: The mappings from v1-style database and retention-policy names onto v2 buckets. THE TRANSLATION LAYER: a v1 query names a database and retention policy, and this is what resolves those to the bucket actually holding the data.

endpoints.name: Database Retention Policy Mapping
endpoints.description: One mapping by id.

endpoints.name: Health
endpoints.description: Whether the instance is healthy. A liveness check.

endpoints.name: Labels
endpoints.description: The labels defined, optionally by organisation. The cross-cutting tagging of buckets, dashboards, tasks and checks -- the only organisational dimension InfluxDB offers besides the organisation itself.

endpoints.name: Label
endpoints.description: One label by id.

endpoints.name: Legacy Authorizations
endpoints.suffix: /legacy/authorizations?authID={Authorization ID?}&org={Organization Name?}&orgID={Organization ID?}&token={Token (Authorization Name)?}&user={User Name?}&userID={User ID?}
endpoints.description: The v1-compatible tokens issued. Present where 1.x tools still write to this instance.

endpoints.name: Legacy Authorization
endpoints.description: One legacy authorization by id.

endpoints.name: Metrics
endpoints.description: The instance's own operational metrics in Prometheus format. NOT the time series data stored in buckets -- this is InfluxDB reporting on itself, and it is the endpoint for questions about the database's own load rather than its contents.

endpoints.name: Notification Endpoints
endpoints.description: Where notifications are delivered -- Slack, PagerDuty, HTTP. Requires an organisation id. The final layer; a rule firing into a dead endpoint is silent.

endpoints.name: Notification Endpoint
endpoints.description: One notification endpoint by id.

endpoints.name: Notification Endpoint Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one notification endpoint.

endpoints.name: Notification Rules
endpoints.description: The rules deciding which check statuses become notifications, filterable by check. The middle layer of alerting.

endpoints.name: Notification Rule
endpoints.description: One notification rule by id.

endpoints.name: Notification Rule Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one notification rule.

endpoints.name: Organizations
endpoints.description: The organisations on the instance. Everything in InfluxDB 2 belongs to an organisation -- buckets, dashboards, tasks, tokens -- so this is the first request and the scope every other one needs.

endpoints.name: Organization
endpoints.description: One organisation by id.

endpoints.name: Organization Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one organisation.

endpoints.name: Organization Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one organisation.

endpoints.name: Ping
endpoints.description: Whether the instance is reachable, and its version. The lightest connectivity check, and the version matters because available endpoints differ between releases.

endpoints.name: Query
endpoints.description: Runs a FLUX query and returns its results. THE DATA ENDPOINT: InfluxDB holds time series, and there is no table to list -- a query defines what comes back, so the question is the request. Requires an organisation. Results come back as annotated CSV rather than JSON, which is the single most surprising thing about this API and means the response needs parsing differently from every other endpoint here.

endpoints.name: Analyze Flux Query
endpoints.description: Checks a Flux query for errors without running it. Sent as a POST with the query in the request body, like the query endpoint itself. Validation rather than data -- useful for confirming a generated query before spending a long-running request on it.

endpoints.name: Generate Abstract Syntax Tree from a Query
endpoints.description: Parses a Flux query into its syntax tree. For tooling that manipulates queries programmatically; of no analytical use.

endpoints.name: Instance Readiness
endpoints.description: Whether the instance has finished starting and is ready to serve. Distinct from health, which reports on a running instance.

endpoints.name: Resources
endpoints.description: The resource types the API exposes. Reference data for building permission sets.

endpoints.name: Routes
endpoints.description: The API's own route listing. A discovery endpoint.

endpoints.name: Notification Rule Array
endpoints.description: The Flux query one notification rule runs. Requires a rule id.

endpoints.name: Scraper Targets
endpoints.suffix: /api/v2/scrapers?id={Scraper Target ID?}&name={Scraper Name ID?}&org={Organization Name?}&orgID={Organization ID?}
endpoints.description: The Prometheus-format endpoints InfluxDB scrapes on a schedule, with their URL and target bucket. Where data arrives without anything writing to InfluxDB explicitly.

endpoints.name: Scraper Target
endpoints.description: One scraper target by id.

endpoints.name: Scraper Target Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one scraper target.

endpoints.name: Scraper Target Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one scraper target.

endpoints.name: Scraper Target Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one scraper target.

endpoints.name: Secret Keys
endpoints.description: The names of the secrets stored for one organisation. Requires an organisation id. Names only -- values are never returned -- and useful for knowing what a task can reference.

endpoints.name: Check Default User, Org, Bucket
endpoints.description: Whether the instance has completed initial setup, and its default user, organisation and bucket. A first-run check.

endpoints.name: Sources
endpoints.description: The data sources configured, optionally by organisation. Connections to other InfluxDB instances.

endpoints.name: Source
endpoints.description: One source by id.

endpoints.name: Source Health
endpoints.description: Whether one source is reachable. Requires a source id.

endpoints.name: Tasks
endpoints.description: The scheduled Flux tasks, with their name, cron or interval, status, and the organisation. TASKS ARE HOW DERIVED DATA IS PRODUCED -- downsampling, alerting, materialised aggregates -- so a bucket that appears to hold suspiciously tidy data usually has a task behind it, and this is where that is visible.

endpoints.name: Task
endpoints.description: One task by id, with its Flux script.

endpoints.name: Task Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one task.

endpoints.name: Task Logs
endpoints.description: The recent log entries across one task's runs. Requires a task id.

endpoints.name: Task Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one task.

endpoints.name: Task Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one task.

endpoints.name: Task Runs
endpoints.description: The execution history of one task, with each run's scheduled time, start and finish, and status. Requires a task id. WHETHER A TASK ACTUALLY RAN is what determines whether the data it produces is complete, and a silently failing task leaves gaps that look like an absence of activity.

endpoints.name: Task Run
endpoints.description: One task run by id, with its outcome.

endpoints.name: Task Run Logs
endpoints.description: The log output of one task run. Requires the task and run ids. Where a failure's cause is found.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Plugins
endpoints.description: The Telegraf plugins available, by type. Reference data.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Configurations
endpoints.description: The Telegraf agent configurations stored, filterable by organisation. Telegraf is the collection agent, so these describe what is being collected and from where -- which explains the shape of the data in a bucket.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Configuration
endpoints.description: One Telegraf configuration by id, with its full TOML.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Configuration Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one Telegraf configuration.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Configuration Members
endpoints.description: The users with member access to one Telegraf configuration.

endpoints.name: Telegraf Configuration Owners
endpoints.description: The users owning one Telegraf configuration.

endpoints.name: Installed Templates
endpoints.description: The template stacks installed on the instance, filterable by organisation. Stacks are bundles of dashboards, tasks and buckets installed together, so this explains resources nobody created individually.

endpoints.name: Stack
endpoints.description: One template stack by id, with the resources it created.

endpoints.name: Current User Feature Flags
endpoints.description: The feature flags in force for the caller. Explains why a documented capability is or is not present.

endpoints.name: Current User
endpoints.description: The account the token belongs to. One record, always the caller -- and the explanation for what the rest of this connector can see, since InfluxDB scopes everything by token permissions.

endpoints.name: Users
endpoints.description: The users on the instance, filterable by id and name. Administrative.

endpoints.name: User
endpoints.description: One user by id.

endpoints.name: Variables
endpoints.description: The dashboard variables defined, each with its query or value list. Variables parameterise dashboard queries, so a cell's query is incomplete without them.

endpoints.name: Variable
endpoints.description: One variable by id.

endpoints.name: Variable Labels
endpoints.description: The labels on one variable.
